'''Marc, Baron Henneaux''' is a Belgian theoretical physicist and professor at the [[Universite libre de Bruxelles]] (ULB) who was born in [[Brussels]] on 5 March 1955.

==Education and career==
{{BLP sources|date=November 2024}}
Henneaux studied physics at ULB and received his doctoral degree in 1980<ref>{{cite web |title=Marc Henneaux. Biographie et publications |url=https://www.college-de-france.fr/fr/chaire/marc-henneaux-champs-cordes-et-gravite-chaire-statutaire/biography |website=Collège de France |language=fr |accessdate=14 November 2024}}</ref> under the supervision of [[Jules Géhéniau]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Marc Henneaux |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1006213 |website=INSPIRE-HEP |accessdate=14 November 2024}}</ref> He was a visiting fellow at [[Princeton University]] for the academic year 1978-1979 where a long-term collaboration with [[Claudio Bunster]] was initiated. He was then postdoctoral research associate and lecturer at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] from 1981 to 1984, to continue working with [[Claudio Bunster]]. From there, he held a research position at the Belgian Science foundation ([[National Fund for Scientific Research|FNRS]]) until 1992, after which he was appointed associate professor at the University of Brussels (1993–1996).

He is currently Full Professor at the University of Brussels since October 1996. He also serves as Director of the [[Solvay Conference|International Solvay Institutes for Physics and Chemistry]], founded by [[Ernest Solvay]] since January 2004. In 2017, Henneaux was appointed Professor at the [[Collège de France]] where he holds the Chair "Champs, Cordes et Gravité".

===Research===
The research of Henneaux is devoted to the study of the theoretical models describing the [[Fundamental interaction|fundamental physical interactions]] ([[electromagnetism]], [[Weak interaction|weak]] and [[Strong interaction|strong]] nuclear forces, [[gravity]]), with a particular emphasis on their [[Symmetry (physics)|symmetries]].  With J. David Brown, he showed that [[General relativity|Einstein's theory of gravity]] in three spacetime dimensions with a negative [[cosmological constant]] possesses a remarkable symmetry structure at infinity described by two [[Virasoro algebra]]s.  The corresponding central charge bears the name of "Brown–Henneaux central charge". This work is sometimes regarded as one of the precursors of the celebrated [[AdS/CFT correspondence]].  Henneaux also studied the geometrical and algebraic aspects of theories with a [[Gauge theory|gauge]] freedom, and in particular on the so-called [[BRST quantization|Becchi–Rouet–Stora–Tyutin symmetry]] and its [[cohomology]]. More recently, in collaboration with [[Thibault Damour]], he showed that hyperbolic [[Coxeter groups]] appear somewhat unexpectedly in gravitational theories and their [[Supergravity|supersymmetric extensions]], in the [[BKL singularity|BKL]] behaviour of the fields near a spacelike singularity.

==Main prizes and awards==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=October 2024}}
* Louis Empain Prize (Belgium) – 1989.
* [[Francqui Prize]] –  2000 (Belgium) – "for his exceptional contributions to our understanding of the forces of Nature", in particular for having "anticipated by more than ten years … a crucial step for understanding the challenge raised by the incorporation of Einstein general relativity in quantum mechanics." (citation of the Jury)
* [[Humboldt Prize|Humboldt Research Award]] (Germany – 2009).
* [[European Research Council|ERC]] Advanced Grant (2011–2015)
* 2014 Bogoliubov Prize of the "Joint Institute for Nuclear Research" (Dubna, Russia), with Valery Rubakov, "for outstanding achievements in theoretical and mathematical physics, promoting international cooperation, and educating young scientists"
* FNRS Quinquennal Prize "Dr A. De Leeuw-Damry-Bourlart" (Fundamental Exact Sciences) (Belgium) for the period 2011–2015
* [[European Research Council|ERC]] Advanced Grant (2016–2021).

==Other distinctions==
* Member of the Royal Academy of Belgium – Since May 2002.
* Francqui Chair – [[Vrije Universiteit Brussel]] – Academic Year 2002–2003.
* Andrejewski Chair – Universities of Leipzig and Jena – May 2003.
* Honorary Degree (Doctor Honoris Causa) – [[University of Craiova]] (Romania) – 2010
* Created "Baron" in 2015 by [[Philippe of Belgium|Philippe, King of the Belgians]].
